source.author: ov
source.text: Quo postquam subiit, nympharum tradidit uni armigerae iaculum pharetramque arcusque retentos; altera depositae subiecit bracchia pallae, vincla duae pedibus demunt; nam doctior illis Ismenis Crocale sparsos per colla capillos colligit in nodum, quamvis erat ipsa solutis.
source.text_original: Quo postquam subiit, nympharum tradidit uni / armigerae iaculum pharetramque arcusque retentos; / altera depositae subiecit bracchia pallae, / vincla duae pedibus demunt; nam doctior illis / Ismenis Crocale sparsos per colla capillos / colligit in nodum, quamvis erat ipsa solutis.
source.text_english: After she had gone in there, she handed her spear, quiver, and unstrung bows to one of the attendant nymphs; another put her arms under the mantle she had laid aside, and two remove the bands from her feet. For Crocale of the Ismenian nymphs, more skilled than the others, gathers her loose hair over her neck into a knot, though she herself had her hair unbound.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: quis tibi, Phrixe, dolor, rapido cum concitus aestu respiceres miserae clamantia virginis ora extremasque manus sparsosque per aequora crines.
reuse.text_original: quis tibi, Phrixe, dolor, rapido cum concitus aestu / respiceres miserae clamantia virginis ora / extremasque manus sparsosque per aequora crines.
reuse.text_english: What grief was yours, Phrixus, when, driven by the rushing swell, you looked back at the face of the wretched maiden, her hands outstretched in her final pleas, and her hair scattered over the waters.
